channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: US War Spending Against Iran Surpasses $47 Billion, Exceeding Pentagon's July Estimate
item.description: US expenditures on the war with Iran have exceeded $47 billion, a figure over 25% higher than the Pentagon's July estimate. These costs include operational expenses for warfare, flight operations, and cyber support, with projected costs for replenishing munitions exceeding $29 billion. Further expenses are anticipated for replacing lost military equipment and repairing damaged US bases.

item.title: Uzbek President to Attend Turkic States Summit in Ankara
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will visit Turkey from October 29-30 to participate in the upcoming summit of the Organization of Turkic States in Ankara. The summit, themed 'Turkic Century: Unity in Language, Thought, and Deed,' will focus on strengthening cooperation in trade, economy, transport, culture, tourism, ecology, and education.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Russia Boost Economic Ties Through Regional and Business Cooperation
item.description: Uzbekistan and Russia are strengthening economic cooperation through increased trade, industrial projects, and direct regional and business ties. Bilateral trade reached $13 billion in 2025, an 8.4% increase. Upcoming events like 'AgroExpo Uzbekistan 2026' aim to foster new business connections and explore new cooperation avenues.

item.title: Over Two Kilograms of Powdered Drug Seized from Suspected Courier in Almaty
item.description: A 25-year-old man suspected of working as a drug courier was detained in Almaty's Nauryzbai district. Police found over a kilogram of suspected mephedrone in a car-sharing vehicle and approximately another kilogram at his residence. Additional hashish weighing about 50 grams was also seized. A criminal case has been initiated.

item.title: Caspian States Convene in Ashgabat to Advance Marine Scientific Research Cooperation
item.description: Turkmenistan hosted a meeting of Caspian Sea littoral states in Ashgabat to discuss cooperation on marine scientific research. Delegates reviewed a draft agreement aimed at facilitating research in the Caspian Sea, where countries aim to develop oil and gas reserves while addressing environmental concerns. The initiative was first proposed in 2018.

item.title: Uzbekistan's New Tashkent Attracts Investors with Favorable Conditions
item.description: An investor shares positive experiences in Uzbekistan's New Tashkent, citing favorable conditions and implemented projects. Despite initial skepticism, Russian entrepreneur Alexander Bakanov has launched four major projects, praising the business environment. The initiative aims to attract $50 billion in investments for projects on a 6,000-hectare area.

item.title: German Publication 'Welt' Highlights Uzbekistan's Cultural Opening to the World
item.description: The German publication 'Welt' notes Uzbekistan's efforts in developing culture, preserving heritage, and promoting national values internationally. The article highlights the growing global interest in Uzbekistan's culture, citing a concert by Lang Lang in Samarkand as an example of its cultural reforms and international engagement.

item.title: Tokayev's Niece Heads New Parliamentary Group 'Children of Kazakhstan'
item.description: Dana Medeuova, niece of President Tokayev, has been appointed head of the new parliamentary group 'Children of Kazakhstan'. The group aims to unite parliamentary efforts to address child protection issues. Medeuova emphasized that child rights are a state policy priority, with a focus on digital safety and equal educational opportunities.

item.title: Taliban-Pakistan Border Clash in Torkham Leaves One Child Dead, Two Aid Workers Injured
item.description: A clash between Taliban forces and Pakistani military personnel in Torkham resulted in the death of one child and injuries to two aid workers. The incident, which began on Wednesday evening, caused a temporary halt to the return of refugees to Afghanistan. Tensions remain high at the border.

item.title: Protest Held in Istanbul After Death of Kazakh Woman
item.description: Activists from the "Socialist Women's Councils" (SKM) protested in Istanbul where a 26-year-old Kazakh woman, Aisulu Bekmakhanova, died. They called her death suspicious, rejecting explanations of suicide or falling. The protest, part of preparations for the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, featured slogans like 'This is not suicide, it is murder.'

item.title: Turkey Seeks to Deepen Strategic Partnership with Kazakhstan, Increase Trade to $15 Billion
item.description: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan expressed his intention to deepen the strategic partnership with Kazakhstan. During his visit to Astana, key documents were signed, including a Declaration of Eternal Friendship and Enhanced Strategic Partnership. Turkey aims to increase bilateral trade to $15 billion and boost investment cooperation in sectors like transport, energy, and AI.

item.title: Thailand Plans 15-Day Visa-Free Regime for Uzbek Citizens
item.description: Thailand is planning to introduce a 15-day visa-free regime for citizens of Uzbekistan. This news digest also includes information on the World Bank allocating $100 million for modernizing Uzbekistan's power grids, Shavkat Mirziyoyev's greetings to participants of the Central Asia International Education Forum, and expected weather changes in Uzbekistan.

item.title: Uzbekistan Expands Cultural Ties with Leading French Institutions
item.description: Uzbekistan's Fund for Cultural Development and Art is strengthening international cooperation and preparing for the 2027 Bukhara Biennale. Meetings with Centre Pompidou leadership resulted in a cooperation agreement for long-term partnership and a future exhibition showcasing Uzbek art. Discussions also took place at Lafayette Anticipations and Fondation Cartier for the upcoming biennale.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev and Turkish President Erdoğan Discuss Future Relations
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev held official talks with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan in Ankara. The leaders discussed the dynamic development of bilateral relations in the spirit of eternal friendship and strategic partnership. Special attention was paid to strengthening trade-economic, investment, and cultural-humanitarian cooperation. They also exchanged views on pressing regional and international issues.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Turkey Aim to Increase Trade Turnover to $15 Billion
item.description: Kazakhstan and Turkey intend to boost their trade turnover to $15 billion and enhance investment cooperation. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated Kazakhstan is ready to support Turkish companies and create favorable business conditions. Turkey is among Kazakhstan's top five trading partners and ten largest investors.

item.title: Uzbek Education Minister Highlights Future Impact of Educational Decisions
item.description: Decisions made in education today shape future economic development and opportunities, according to Uzbek Minister of Education and Science Erkin Turdimov at the Central Asia International Education Forum in Tashkent. He stressed the importance of regional cooperation for practical results, improving learning quality, and unlocking youth potential in a rapidly changing global economy.

item.title: Kazakh-Turkish Relations Reach 'Eternal Friendship' Level, Presidents Meet
item.description: Kazakhstan and Turkey's relations have reached a level of 'eternal friendship,' according to President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev during expanded talks with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan. Tokayev highlighted shared history and language, emphasizing mutual trust and the absence of disagreements. He congratulated Erdoğan on Turkey's Republic Day, praising his leadership and Turkey's growing international influence.

item.title: Ecologists Explain Cause of Air Pollution in Tashkent
item.description: Ecologists have explained the cause of air pollution in Tashkent. Windless weather and temperature inversions observed in Central Asia during October led to the accumulation of harmful particles in the atmosphere. The article provides further details on the phenomenon.

item.title: Germany Deports 40 Criminal Migrants to Afghanistan
item.description: Germany's Interior Ministry confirmed the deportation of 40 "criminal migrants" to Afghanistan. The individuals, including those convicted of sexual offenses, violence, and drug trafficking, were reportedly sent directly from prison. Germany has increased such deportations following an agreement with the Taliban, while human rights groups and UN experts express concerns.

item.title: Cassation Court Overturns Sentence for Former Shymkent National Security Deputy Chief
item.description: Kazakhstan's Cassation Court has overturned the 12-year sentence for Manat Sarbasov, former deputy head of the National Security Committee in Shymkent, who was convicted of bribery and money laundering. The court cited significant violations of criminal procedure. The case will be retried in a specialized court, and the ruling applies to all defendants.

item.title: Turkey Welcomes President Tokayev with Kazakh Language Greetings During State Visit
item.description: Ankara, Turkey, prepared a warm welcome for Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's official visit. Electronic screens displayed portraits of both leaders, and buildings were adorned with the flags of Kazakhstan and Turkey. President Tokayev was personally greeted by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan at Etimesgut Airport. Greetings in Kazakh were displayed on city screens.

item.title: Bus Hits Girl in Astana; Three Passengers Injured During Sudden Braking
item.description: A bus in Astana struck a young girl, and three passengers sustained injuries due to sudden braking. All four individuals were transported to the hospital. Eyewitnesses reported the girl ran into the road unexpectedly. Police confirmed the incident, stating the pedestrian crossed the road improperly. An investigation is underway.

item.title: Uzbek Citizens Face Increased Scrutiny at Foreign Borders Amidst New Entry Rules
item.description: Uzbek citizens are experiencing heightened checks at international borders, with countries like Thailand, Montenegro, and Egypt implementing new entry regulations. Some Uzbeks are being denied entry and turned back. This trend raises questions about why Uzbeks are becoming 'unwanted' guests as Uzbekistan opens up to the world.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Turkey Affirm Commitment to Deepen Strategic Partnership
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Turkey's President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan held talks, focusing on strengthening economic, investment, and cultural-humanitarian ties. Both leaders expressed satisfaction with the consistent development of bilateral relations in the spirit of friendship and strategic partnership. They also exchanged views on current international and regional issues.

item.title: Uzbekistan Allocates State Funds for Compensation to Victims of 'Dok-1 Max' Drug Case
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Health announced compensation payments to families of children affected by 'Dok-1 Max' and 'Ambronol' drugs. The Bureau of Compulsory Enforcement had only recovered 20% of the 82 billion soums owed. President Mirziyoyev directed the release of the remaining 65.2 billion soums from the state budget to expedite payments to 88 families.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Begins Receiving Fuel Shipments from China via Railway
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has started receiving fuel and lubricants from China via railway, according to Kanatbek Eshatov, president of the Oil Traders Association. While fuel imports previously came mainly from Russia, Kyrgyzstan now sources them from Azerbaijan, Turkmenistan, Belarus, and Turkey. The country is experiencing a slight gasoline deficit and seeking diverse suppliers.

item.title: Ankara Welcomes Kazakh President Tokayev with Grand Preparations for Official Visit
item.description: Ankara displayed large portraits of Presidents Tokayev and Erdogan, along with flags of Kazakhstan and Turkey, and bilingual greetings. Turkish President Erdogan personally greeted the Kazakh leader upon arrival at Etimesgut Airport. The extensive preparations in the Turkish capital highlighted the significance of the official visit.

item.title: Honor Guard, Cavalry, and Artillery Salutes Greet Tokayev in Ankara
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev received a ceremonial welcome, including an honor guard, cavalry escort, and artillery salutes, upon his arrival at the Presidential Palace in Ankara for an official visit to Turkey. State anthems were played, followed by bilateral talks in a limited format with President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Tokayev Awards Citizens on Republic Day
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has awarded a large group of Kazakh citizens for their significant contributions to the country's development. The awards ceremony, held on Republic Day, involved numerous state officials. Notably, leaders of supposedly independent public and party structures also participated in presenting the state awards.

item.title: Munira Aminova Appointed Chairperson of Uzbekistan's Higher Attestation Commission
item.description: Munira Aminova has been appointed the new Chairperson of the Higher Attestation Commission (HAC) under the Academy of Sciences of Uzbekistan. Previously, she served as the rector of the International Agricultural University and an advisor to the Minister of Foreign Affairs. Aminova holds a doctorate in political science and has extensive experience in public administration and higher education.

item.title: Russia strengthens ties with Taliban, moving towards closer partnership
item.description: Russia is deepening its engagement with the Taliban regime in Afghanistan, shifting from dialogue to becoming a close foreign partner. This policy accelerated in 2025, marked by the suspension of the ban on Taliban activities and increased economic and political relations. Experts view this as a fundamental change in Moscow's approach to the group.

item.title: Italy's Eni Ranks Countries by Oil Reserves, Including Central Asia
item.description: Italian company Eni has released a ranking of countries with the largest oil reserves. The report includes data on Uzbekistan and other Central Asian nations, detailing their respective oil reserves. The ranking aims to provide a comprehensive overview of global oil resources.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Presidential Affairs Administration Acquires Kylym Bank
item.description: The Administration of the President of Kyrgyzstan has become the owner of 100% of Kylym Bank's shares. Previously, the entire stake belonged to the Ministry of Finance. President Sadyr Japarov signed a decree in August to transfer the bank, aiming to improve its operational efficiency.

item.title: Dragon Oil to Increase Turkmenistan Production to 200,000 Barrels Daily by 2030
item.description: Dragon Oil plans to boost production at its 'Çeleken' contract area to 200,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day by 2030 and extend its partnership with Turkmenistan beyond 2035. The company's investments in the country have reached nearly $12 billion. Dragon Oil has been operating in Turkmenistan since May 2000.

item.title: Six Wagons of Coal Delivered to Belovodskoye Village in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Six wagons of coal have been delivered to the village of Belovodskoye in the Chuy region of Kyrgyzstan. OAO 'Kyrgyzkomur' reported that the solid fuel is of good quality and is already being purchased by local residents. The country plans to regulate coal prices for 90 days.

item.title: Head of Samruk-Energy replaced due to slow investment project execution
item.description: The head of Samruk-Energy has been replaced due to unsatisfactory progress in implementing strategic investment projects and insufficient oversight of new generation capacity construction timelines. Qairat Makstov, who led the company since June 2023, was removed by the board of directors.

item.title: Uzbek President Mirziyoyev to attend Turkic States Organization summit in Ankara
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will visit Turkey on October 29-30 for an official visit. He will participate in the upcoming summit of the Organization of Turkic States in Ankara, themed "Turkic Century: Unity in Language, Thought, and Action." The summit will discuss expanding cooperation in trade, economy, investment, transport, and culture.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev to Visit Turkey for Turkic States Summit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will pay a working visit to Turkey on October 29-30. The head of state will participate in the next summit of the Organization of Turkic States in Ankara, themed 'Turkic Century: Unity in Language, Thought, and Action'.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Chess Team Secures Second Gold Medal at FIDE Olympiad
item.description: Uzbekistan's national chess team won its second gold medal at the FIDE Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, losing only one match. Star player Javokhir Sindarov will challenge the world champion in November. The team, including top-ranked players like Nodirbek Abdusattorov and Nodirbek Yakubboev, defeated strong opponents such as India, China, and the United States.

item.title: US Promotes Small Nuclear Reactor Technology in Caucasus and Central Asia
item.description: The United States is actively promoting its small modular nuclear reactor (SMR) technology in the Caucasus and Central Asia. US Deputy Assistant Secretary of State Shawna J. Wilson met with Armenian and Kazakh officials to discuss nuclear cooperation. Both countries have shown openness to the idea, with Armenia finalizing a deal and Kazakhstan signing an agreement for training assistance.
